title: Musician in Residence appointed for 2026
subtitle: Oktoberfest noise exemption, new parking prohibitions, and a development charge complaint hearing adjourned to September
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee met briefly and recommended appointing Amanda Braam as the City's 2026 Artist in Residence, focused on music. The residency centres on an intergenerational songwriting project that brings together youth and older adults and ends in a community concert. The vote was {{vote:m4}}.

The committee also recommended a noise exemption for K-W Oktoberfest Inc. so events at various clubs and locations can run from September 25 to October 17, 2026 {{vote:m1}}. It recommended new parking prohibitions on Fergus Avenue, Greenfield Avenue and West Avenue, with the Uniform Traffic By-law to be amended {{vote:m2}}.
The committee agreed to adjourn the Section 20 development charge complaint jurisdiction hearing for 15 Dellroy Avenue to no later than September 14, 2026 {{vote:m3}}.
These are committee recommendations. Council must still adopt them before they take effect.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended appointing Amanda Braam as the 2026 Artist in Residence and authorizing the Mayor and Clerk to sign an agreement with the artist.
The committee recommended granting K-W Oktoberfest Inc. an exemption from the Noise by-law for events at various clubs and locations from September 25 to October 17, 2026.
The committee recommended prohibiting parking on sections of Fergus Avenue, Greenfield Avenue and West Avenue and amending the Uniform Traffic By-law accordingly.
The committee agreed to adjourn the jurisdiction hearing on the Section 20 development charge complaint to no later than September 14, 2026.

debate: The consent items and the development charge adjournment drew no questions or discussion from the committee.
Staff said the jury favoured the proposal for its emphasis on intergenerational connection, community building, accessibility and relationship development through music.
Staff said the call drew many eligible submissions and was assessed by a jury that included an Arts and Culture Advisory Committee representative and music industry professionals.
The appointee said youth and older adults tend to be separated in the local music scene, and that writing songs together could help each group learn from the other.
One councillor congratulated the appointee, citing earlier performances at Neighbours Day and in a local music series, and moved the appointment.
